Mr Chris Sammons, Head of School Mr Matthew Seddon, Secondary Principal

content.text:
Both are well-regarded British-curriculum schools for ages 2–18 in the Sukhumvit area. The biggest difference is what students take in the last two years: Patana offers the IB Diploma, while Bangkok Prep offers A Levels.

## Who runs them and how big they are
- **Bangkok Patana:** It's
non-selective and not-for-profit, and Thailand's first and largest British international school
. It has
2,300+ students from Nursery to Year 13, from 68 different nationalities, 20% of them Thai
Thai students are capped at 20%

of places.
- **Bangkok Prep:** It's
privately owned
and
part of the ISP group
, with about
1,800 students
. Unlike Patana, it gives applicants an assessment:
sessions run from 30 minutes to 3 hours depending on the child's year level

.

## Curriculum after age 16
- **Patana:**
95% of students take the full IB Diploma

. There's also an IB Career-related Programme that combines a BTEC diploma with some IB courses.
- **Bangkok Prep:**
In Years 12–13, students specialise in A Level courses
. It also offers
BTEC Levels 1 & 2 and the BTEC Level 3 Extended Diploma

.

The IB means studying six subjects broadly. A Levels mean going deep in about three. That choice matters more than small differences in results.

## 2025 exam results
- **Patana:**
66% of (I)GCSE results were grades 7–9, and the average IB score was 35.0

(it was 36 in 2024).
- **Bangkok Prep:**
58% of IGCSE grades were 9–7. At A Level, 52% of grades were A*/A and 72% were A*–B.
That's a big improvement on
2024: 46% at 9–7 for IGCSE and 35% A*/A at A Level

.
- **University places:** both sent students to top US universities in 2025, including Brown, Cornell, NYU and UCLA. Bangkok Prep also sent students to Imperial College in the UK.

Patana's IGCSE results are a bit higher, which is notable because it doesn't select students. Bangkok Prep's results are rising.

## Campus and activities
- **Patana:** A large green campus on Sukhumvit 105 (Bang Na).
It has over 200 extracurricular activities
, including Model UN, Duke of Edinburgh and Habitat for Humanity. The commute is a common complaint: one parent review called
"the location challenging with lots of traffic"

and the school large and impersonal. That's one opinion, but worth checking for yourself.
- **Bangkok Prep:** The Good Schools Guide praises
its unique forest campus and strong community spirit
. The secondary campus on Sukhumvit 77 is
close to On Nut BTS station
. The school used to split primary and secondary between Sukhumvit 53 and 77. One recent source says
everything is now on Sukhumvit 77

, so confirm this with the school.

## Fees
Third-party estimates disagree, so ask both schools for their official fee schedules.
- **Patana:**
THB 595,100 in Year 1 up to THB 796,600 in Year 13
, with
lunch included for Nursery to Year 6

.
- **Bangkok Prep:** Listed at
. On top of that are one-off
registration fees: THB 120,000 for Early Years, THB 160,000 for Years 1–6 and THB 110,000 for Years 7–12

.

Yearly tuition is broadly similar. Check the one-off joining fees at both schools, as they can add a lot to the first-year cost.

## Which might suit you
- **Patana** fits if you want the IB Diploma, a non-selective not-for-profit school, a very large campus and a huge choice of activities, and you can handle the Bang Na commute.
- **Bangkok Prep** fits if your child would do better focusing on fewer subjects at A Level (or wants a BTEC route), you want a smaller school with a closer community, or you live near On Nut or central Sukhumvit.

If you tell me your child's age, where you'd live, and whether you prefer the IB or A Levels, I can narrow this down.
